translations.text: The elder, to dear Gaius, whom I love in truth.
Dear friend, I pray for you to prosper in everything and be healthy, just as your soul prospers.
For I was very glad when brothers came and testified to your faithfulness to the truth, telling how you live in the truth.
I have no greater joy than this: to hear that my children are living in the truth.
Dear friend, you act faithfully in whatever you do for the brothers, especially those who are strangers.
They have testified to your love before the whole church. You do well to provide for their journey in a manner worthy of God.
For they went out for the sake of his name, taking nothing from the Gentiles.
We therefore ought to welcome people like these, so that we may be helpers of the truth.
I wanted to write to the church, but Diotrephes, who loves to be first among them, does not accept us.

For this reason, if I come, I will call attention to what he has done, attacking us with malicious words. Not content with this, he does not welcome the brothers himself, and he stops those who welcome them and puts them out of the church.
Dear friend, do not imitate evil, but good. Whoever does good is from God. Whoever does evil has not seen God.
Everyone testifies on behalf of Demetrius, as do the church and the truth itself. We also testify, and you know that our testimony is true.
I had many things to write to you, but I do not want to write to you with ink and pen.
But I hope to see you soon, and we will speak face to face.
Peace be with you. The friends greet you. Greet the friends, each one by name.
